thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY] requests a quote for re-registering its WX-PS200 product after its Bluetooth module reached EOL and is being replaced with a successor module using a different chip, while wanting to preserve continuity with the existing Declaration ID. The consultant determines that profile testing is unnecessary (since the successor module's QDID already covers the existing product's supported profiles), that RF testing necessity depends on the successor module's antenna configuration, and proactively discloses that the successor module's QDID carries forward several inter-layer Mandatory-dependency findings from its original registration under an older system -- which do not block the new registration but will be inherited by it. The thread closes with the standard Review Page confirmation and compliance folder document request.
all_questions_found: What is the successor module's QDID/DN, and what is the full list of profiles the product supports?
Does the successor module's QDID already cover the existing product's supported profiles, making profile testing unnecessary?
Does RF testing need to be performed for the successor module, and does that depend on its antenna configuration (built-in, connector, or external)?
Does the successor module's QDID carry forward inter-layer consistency findings from when it was originally registered, and if so, does that block the new registration?
Will the customer's own new registration also inherit those same inter-layer consistency findings?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread illustrates how to scope a re-registration for an EOL-driven module replacement when the customer wants to preserve continuity with an existing Declaration ID: profile testing can be skipped if the successor module's QDID already covers the existing product's supported profiles, while RF testing necessity depends specifically on the successor module's antenna configuration (built-in antenna or antenna connector exempts RF testing; an external-antenna module requires full RF item testing). It also covers how an older module QDID's inter-layer consistency findings (Mandatory dependency rules across BB, L2CAP, LL, and LMP tied to HFP and GAP items) can be inherited from when that QDID was originally registered under an earlier system, without blocking a new registration that references it -- though the new registration will carry forward those same findings.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: When a customer replaces an EOL module with a successor module while wanting to preserve registration continuity, check whether the successor module's QDID already covers the existing product's supported profiles (if so, profile testing is unnecessary) and check the successor module's antenna configuration to determine RF testing scope (built-in/connector antenna exempts RF testing; external antenna requires it). Separately, an older module QDID may carry forward inter-layer consistency findings from its original registration under a since-superseded system; these do not block a new registration that references it, but should be proactively disclosed to the customer since their own registration will inherit the same findings.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming full testing is required without checking whether the successor module's QDID already covers existing profiles, or without checking its antenna configuration, would lead to over-quoting unnecessary tests. Failing to proactively disclose inherited inter-layer consistency findings from an older module QDID could surprise the customer later when they notice the same findings appear in their own new registration.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When scoping a re-registration for an EOL module replacement with continuity requirements, check the successor module's QDID against the existing product's supported profiles (to determine profile-test necessity) and its antenna configuration (to determine RF-test necessity), rather than assuming full testing is required. When an older module QDID carries forward inter-layer consistency findings from its original registration, proactively disclose this to the customer rather than letting them discover it themselves -- it does not block the new registration, but it will be inherited by it.
